question: Stripe and PayPal official evidence for customer-visible refund credit versus merchant accounting terminal states, disputes, and expired captures (S15).

scope.method: Public documentation reading only; each layer kept separate; undocumented windows remain unknown.

claims.claim: Stripe describes card customer-visible refund timing as approximately 5-10 business days depending on the bank, while also stating successful refunds appear on statements in real time depending on card network and issuer.

sources.support: Trace a refund section states approximately 5-10 business days; Refund requests section states real-time statement appearance depending on network and issuer.

claims.caveat: The two official formulations preserve issuer/network variation; no single exact issuer-independent timestamp.

claims.claim: Shortly issued Stripe refunds can appear as a reversal: the original charge drops from the customer statement and no separate credit is issued.

sources.support: Refund and reversal section directly describes reversal statement behavior.

claims.caveat: A reversal is not a separately posted refund credit.

claims.claim: Stripe says failed refunds return the amount from the bank to Stripe, add it back to Stripe balance, and can take up to 30 days from requesting the refund.
claims.caveat: This is the failed-refund balance-return path, not a normal successful-refund balance settlement window.

claims.claim: ACH Direct Debit refunds are asynchronous and take up to 3 business days; success transitions Refund to succeeded and failure to failed, with failure amount returned to Stripe balance.

sources.support: ACH Refunds and Tracking refunds sections.

claims.caveat: The 3-business-day statement is processing time; the page does not give a separate bank-visible posting window.

claims.claim: ACH refunds are separate credits to the customer bank account, never reversals, and are not explicitly labeled refund on the bank statement.
claims.caveat: Customer-visible independent timing is unknown in the official page.

claims.claim: SEPA refunds typically take 3-4 business days to process and funds arrive in the customer account within 5 business days.
claims.caveat: Processing and customer-account arrival are separate statements; no normal Stripe balance return window is stated.

claims.claim: SEPA dispute is no-questions-asked up to eight weeks; after eight weeks and up to 13 months, only unauthorized disputes are allowed; SEPA disputes are final with no appeal process.

sources.support: Disputes section directly states windows and no appeal.

claims.claim: Bacs refunds typically take 3-4 business days and must be submitted within 180 days; Bacs disputes have no set time limit and are final and cannot be appealed.
claims.caveat: The page gives processing time, not a separate customer statement-visibility deadline.

claims.claim: Stripe PayPal payments can be refunded up to 180 days; depending on settlement preference Stripe uses Stripe balance or PayPal balance/available PayPal funding.
claims.caveat: No customer-visible refund window or final balance timing is directly stated there; those remain unknown.

claims.claim: For general Stripe card disputes, response window is usually 7-21 days depending on card network; submitted response is final and cannot be amended; lost dispute refund is permanent.
claims.caveat: Stripe itself qualifies the window as usually and network-dependent; no uniform cross-network appeal rule inferred.

claims.claim: Stripe PayPal disputes may be filed within 180 calendar days; requested evidence is due in 2-19 calendar days by category; PayPal aims to decide within 30 calendar days after evidence; some lost disputes can be appealed by PayPal but Stripe does not support appeals.
claims.caveat: Appeal availability is case-dependent and handled through PayPal, not a universal reversible state.

claims.claim: Stripe says if authorization expires before capture, funds are released and payment status changes to canceled; a requires_capture PaymentIntent cannot be directly refunded and must be canceled.
claims.caveat: Official text confirms release/cancel, not automatic creation of a refund; automatic refund is unknown.

claims.claim: PayPal Payments v2 refund_status values are CANCELLED, FAILED, PENDING, and COMPLETED; the schema does not define refund status SUCCEEDED.
claims.caveat: COMPLETED is an object field value; it is not evidence of a same-named webhook event.

claims.claim: PayPal Payments v2 capture status values include COMPLETED, DECLINED, PARTIALLY_REFUNDED, PENDING, REFUNDED, and FAILED.
claims.caveat: Capture statuses must not be substituted for refund object statuses.

claims.claim: PayPal official webhook list includes PAYMENT.CAPTURE.COMPLETED, PAYMENT.CAPTURE.REFUNDED, PAYMENT.REFUND.PENDING, PAYMENT.REFUND.FAILED, PAYMENT.CAPTURE.REVERSED, and PAYMENT.AUTHORIZATION.VOIDED; it does not list PAYMENT.REFUND.COMPLETED or PAYMENT.REFUND.SUCCEEDED in the Payments v2 section.

sources.support: Payments v2 webhook event names and descriptions.

claims.caveat: Absence is bounded to the official list and Payments v2 scope; capture/refund event names remain distinct.

claims.claim: PayPal documents authorization void/cancel separately from capture refund; authorization reaching its 30-day validity period can trigger PAYMENT.AUTHORIZATION.VOIDED.

sources.support: Payments v2 operations and official webhook event list link.

claims.caveat: Official text does not say authorization expiry automatically creates a refund; automatic refund remains unknown.

claims.claim: PayPal official help says an un-escalated dispute automatically closes after 20 days and closed disputes cannot be reopened or escalated to a claim.

sources.support: Official consumer Resolution Center help page.

claims.caveat: This consumer help workflow is not generalized to all Payments v2 merchant refund/capture flows.

claims.claim: Officially specified independent customer-visible windows for Stripe ACH, Stripe Bacs, Stripe PayPal, and PayPal REST refund completion are not stated in the reviewed primary pages; normal successful Stripe/PayPal balance final-return windows are likewise not stated.
claims.caveat: Semantic=unknown: absence of a directly stated window in the reviewed official pages is not proof that no provider-specific operational window exists elsewhere.

claims.claim: A cross-platform, all-country, all-payment-method rule that dispute resolution or appeal is reversible is not established by the reviewed official sources.
claims.caveat: Semantic=unknown: only payment-method-specific and flow-specific explicit rules are recorded.

areas: Stripe card/ACH/SEPA/Bacs/PayPal refund timing and layered states
PayPal Payments v2 REST refund/capture status fields
payment-method-specific dispute deadlines and appeal text
Stripe and PayPal expired authorization release/void versus refund distinction
known_unknowns: independent ACH/Bacs/PayPal customer-visible bank or wallet posting windows
normal successful refund balance finalization timing
